question: Does malloc_trim(0) return the free arena that trim_threshold cannot reach? No recorded arm had asked: every allocator arm configured GLIBC_TUNABLES, and trim_threshold trims only the top of an arena on free().
preregistered_prediction: post-trim G3 lands at 40-150 MiB, i.e. the gate as literally written passes. Failure mode named in advance: glibc returns only whole free pages, so 750k retired small objects could leave one live object per page.
preregistered_decision_rule: If post-trim is under 256 MiB in all rounds, shedding is demoted from required-for-G3 to required-for-the-peak, and a peak criterion must be argued for rather than the pass being banked.
result: Prediction beaten. Post-trim G3 is 10.2 / 12.4 / 14.2 MiB, 25x UNDER the 256 MiB budget rather than 1.86x over. 454-466 MiB is returned per round. The fragmentation failure mode did not occur.
identity_check: Live heap holds at 17.0-17.2 MiB across all three rounds while RSS falls to 23.5-27.4 MiB, so RSS is live heap plus overhead and the returned pages are genuinely with the kernel.
the_half_that_is_not_a_win: malloc_trim does not touch the traversal peak, which stays at 489.0-492.6 MiB with 750,438 live views. G3 measures what is left after release; running on modest hardware depends on what is held during it. A gate that a process passes while its high-water mark sits at half a gigabyte is not measuring what it was written to measure.
consequence: Shedding moves from required-for-G3 to required-for-the-peak and for survivability under a memory cap. That is a difference of weeks. G3 needs a sibling criterion on VmHWM, and the cgroup survivability arm should become a hard gate rather than a nice-to-have. This tightens the gate; it arrived from a result that looks superficially like a pass.
limits: One run, three rounds. This establishes a large effect well outside the 6 percent between-run variation of retained RSS, not a precise figure.

The trim is called from an LD_PRELOAD interposer at a quiescent fixture marker. A shipped trim must be idle-gated and its cost measured; earlier data records 20-26 ms median and 62 ms maximum at around 1 GB.
Zero-length files throughout. No content mappings are held.
